messages:
Amanda: Quick check — pdx3 (GCP) cutover scheduled tomorrow 10:00 PDT. Need confirmation on egress IP block + BGP ASN and final owner list. PR: https://github.com/redwood/infra/pull/4826
Chris: I can own the BGP side. Which ASN are we using for pdx3, and do we need a distinct announcement policy?
Amanda: We're using ASN 64513 for pdx3 (keeps parity with other GCP edges). Egress block assigned by netops: 35.234.10.0/24. Need network signoff before merge.
Jordan: Heads up — PR touches kube-proxy config. I left a comment about avoiding the iptables full flush during rollout.
infra-bot: CI: infra/4826 — build passed, staging smoke OK (tests: 128/128).
Lee: I can take KMS ownership for pdx3. Reminder: keys must be provisioned in the region before we start traffic-shift.
Chris: Ack. I'll coordinate key creation with you, Lee. Who is acting as primary oncall for the window?
Samantha: I'm oncall 09:30-11:30 PDT tomorrow, available for cutover. I'll monitor SLAs and error budgets.
Amanda: Runbook updated: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/ENG/pages/PDX3-Cutover. See section 'traffic-shift' — TL;DR steps and rollback criteria.
Amanda: Snippet for creating static address (for reference):
```
gcloud compute addresses create egress-pdx3 --addresses=35.234.10.5 --region=us-west3
```
Kevin: Small nit: healthchecks need explicit accept rules on the host. Example: `iptables -A INPUT -p tcp --dport 8080 -s 10.0.0.0/8 -j ACCEPT` — otherwise probes might fail during warmup.
Jordan: @Kevin good catch. Can we gate that behind the nodepool rollout? I don't want to open wide rules cluster-wide.
Kevin: We can scope by subnet tag, will PR a discrete change to infra if y'all prefer.
Chris: Fallback plan question — if our BGP session to GCP fails, do we have an automated failover to usw1 announcements or do we keep sessions but shift at proxy?
Amanda: Fallback policy: prefer pdx3 -> usw1 -> edge-proxy. If BGP withdraws, we announce backup /24 from usw1 (automated via netops playbook). If proxy health drops, we shift at the proxy layer. Both are scripted in the runbook.
Jordan: I'll review PR today and ping reviewers (@Lee @Kevin). Trying to keep the thread light — any blocking legal/compliance items on data residency for pdx3?
Lee: Data residency: KMS in-region + audit logs retention policy applied. Legal already signed off on the region template last week. No extra docs required.
Chris: Added one more detail to the PR — BGP community tags so our monitoring can auto-classify pdx3 announcements.
Amanda: Thanks. Final preflight checklist I'm monitoring: 1) PR merged (infra/4826) 2) KMS keys created in pdx3 3) BGP sessions up and /24 announced 4) Staging smoke + canary pass 5) Traffic-shift monitor green for 15m. I'll post status updates here during the window. :white_check_mark:
Jordan: Reviewed + left one comment about kube-proxy flag ordering. Not blocking.
Lee: KMS key ring created (placeholder name: projects/redwood/locations/us-west3/keyRings/pdx3-kr). Will hand credentials to netops for the cutover.
Samantha: I'll take first 30m of monitoring and escalate if error rate > 1% or latency spike > 200ms.
infra-bot: Reminder: scheduled maintenance window booked for 2026-03-18 10:00 PDT.
Amanda: All right — permissions and owners assigned. @Chris please post when BGP announced, @Jordan when PR merges, @Lee when keys are ready. I'll coordinate the shift. :shipit:
